target_customer: Professional filmmakers, studios, agencies and indie creators producing AI-assisted video
problem: Generative video work is scattered across many models and tools with no shared workspace, provenance tracking or cost control, which makes professional collaboration messy.
business_model: SaaS subscription with a free tier, paid plans from $15 per month and extra credits for some generative models; bring-your-own fal API key

founders.name: Koh Terai
founders.background_notes: Cinematographer whose work screened at Cannes Directors' Fortnight per the YC page. The YC page also mentions a CS background; a search snippet reported an NYU Abu Dhabi degree, not confirmed on a page I opened.

competitors.name: Runway
competitors.what: Broad AI video generation and editing workspace
competitors.traction_then: Described as the broadest AI video workspace in 2026 comparison posts

competitors.name: Google Flow
competitors.what: Scene-led AI filmmaking tool, positioned as a Figma for filmmaking
competitors.traction_then: Plan-based credits; availability varied by region

competitors.name: LTX Studio
competitors.what: Full production platform with storyboarding, multi-scene management and timeline
competitors.traction_then: Vendor comparison pages describe it as the most comprehensive option

competitors.name: Higgsfield
competitors.traction_then: Low-priced generation, positioned as a generation tool more than a production platform

technical_complexity.rationale: Martini does not train models. The work is a multiplayer timeline, orchestration of many third-party video models, shot lineage tracking, spend analytics and XML export to Premiere and Resolve, which is standard but broad product engineering for a team of two.

defensibility.rationale: It wraps third-party models and well-funded players such as Runway and Google Flow can add collaboration features. Possible lock-in comes from project history, provenance and team workflows, but this is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of the late 2026 sources opened, no acquisition or copy aimed specifically at Martini was found.

market_need_then: Generative video models proliferated through 2025, and professionals wanted a workflow that fits editing tools (XML export), shared review and cost control. Evidence is the product framing on the YC page and the July 2026 No Film School coverage; no sourced spend data.

branding.domain_note: Uses martini.film, not a .com. The company entity is listed as C47 Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and professional with playful touches such as '0 olives used' next to billing info and the CTO tagline 'Turns Martinis into Films'.

branding.brand_signature: Cocktail and olive wordplay tied to the film term 'Martini shot' is plausible but no source states it; the visible signature is the olive joke.
branding.community_and_virality: Sponsored AI credits at a June 2026 Singapore AI video workshop and spoke at an NAB Show session in 2026; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable and filmic name but it is a common word; coverage found is mostly about the product (No Film School, NAB Show), not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Martini is a Winter 2026 YC company that is still active and very early, so no outcome exists yet. It pairs a cinematographer CEO with a former Supabase growth engineer and sells a collaborative workspace on top of third-party video models. The main risks are model-platform bundling by Runway or Google and thin defensibility, while the distribution through professional film events and a free tier are early positives. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found in an outcome search.
notes: Funding: aggregators (Neuronfeed $500K seed January 2026, VCBacked pre-seed March 2026) conflict on stage and date and no primary source confirms them, so they are unverified and not recorded as a round. The competitor sources are 2026 vendor comparison posts, so dates are approximate. Founder education for Koh Terai beyond the YC page is unverified.
